## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

Load libraries

```{r}
## load libraries ##
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(kableExtra)

## load data ##
glimpse(penguins)

## clean data ##
palmer_clean <- penguins |>
  select(species,sex,year,bill_length_mm,body_mass_g)
glimpse(palmer_clean)

```

```{r}
## ggplot ##
#|out-width:70% # changes the size of your figure
ggplot(data=palmer_clean,mapping = aes(x=species, y=bill_length_mm))+
  geom_boxplot()
```

```{r}
## ggplot ##
#|fig-width: 3 # inputs exact size (inches) of figure
#|fig-width: 5
ggplot(data=palmer_clean,mapping = aes(x=species, y=bill_length_mm))+
  geom_boxplot()


```

```{r}

## ggplot ##
#| fig-align:"center" # puts figure in the center of the rendering
ggplot(data=palmer_clean,mapping = aes(x=species, y=bill_length_mm))+
  geom_boxplot()

```

## Coding a table

```{r}
penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(billmean = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  kbl() # make it a kable table
```

## Making it fancy

```{r}
penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(billmean = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  kbl()  |> # make it a kable table
  kable_classic() |> # add a theme
  row_spec(2, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "red") |> # highlight row 2
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) # don't make it so wide
```

## Cross Referencing

One of Quarto’s biggest advantages for scientific writing: figures and tables are auto-numbered and linkable from your prose. Step 1: Give your chunk a label starting with fig-

```{r}
#| label: fig-penguin-bill
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: Bill length vs. bill depth for three penguin species.

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_depth_mm, y = bill_length_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_viridis_d()
```

Step 2: Reference it anywhere in your prose with @fig-penguin-bill

As shown in @fig-penguin-bill, bill dimensions differ clearly by species.

# Cross-references:Tables

```{r}
#| label: tbl-penguin-means
#| tbl-cap: "Mean bill length by species."

penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(mean_bill = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  kbl()
```

Mean bill lengths are summarised in @tbl-penguin-means.

Prefix rules

- Figures must use a fig- prefix — label: fig-my-plot
- Tables must use a tbl- prefix — label: tbl-my-table
- Quarto will error if the prefix doesn’t match the cross-reference type

# Activity: Cross-references

In your Quarto document: \* Create a code chunk that makes a ggplot — give it a fig- label and a fig-cap:

```{r}
#| label: fig-penguin-sex
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Penguin Sex vs. Bill Length for three penguin species.

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = sex, y = bill_length_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_color_viridis_d()
```

- Create a code chunk that makes a kbl() table — give it a tbl- label and a tbl-cap:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-penguin-means-2
#| tbl-cap: "Mean body mass by species and year"

penguins |>
  group_by(year,species) |>
  summarise(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = mean_mass)|>
  kbl()|>
  kable_classic()

```

The mean body mass of penguins varied among species and years (see @tbl-penguin-means-2).

- In a prose paragraph, reference both with @fig-... and @tbl-...

The mean body mass varied among species and years, as shown in Table 1 @tbl-penguin-means-2. Figure @fig-bill-length shows the patterns of bill length in relation to sex among the three species.

- Render and confirm Figure 1 and Table 1 appear as clickable cross-links
